status: conditional temporal-credit arithmetic and comparison proposals; no eligibility rule selected
value_lineage: C-15/P-29 uses preceding context to predict observed tokens; C-26/P-61 preserves useful history and C-24/P-54 distinguishes dominant response duration from individual dynamics. H-74 forbids adding a trace merely because a literature algorithm has one.
assumptions: Tokens arrive every T seconds in the first reference. Token-level indicator vectors are used only to derive a credit mixture, not as the application neuron encoding.

Each previous unit input contributes an additive exponential tail with half-life H, no saturation, noise, cancellation, contextual assignment or interaction. Infinite-past formulas are stationary references; finite starts have shorter sums.
Using H=0.5 seconds illustrates overlap. The user specifies a loose dominant-token response objective, not a universal per-neuron exponential leak or a selected learning window.

A hypothetical update uses pre-input source c_n and the independently observed token responsibility y_n. Available edges and a correlation update are assumed for the arithmetic; no growth or learning law is adopted.

symmetric_coactivity.equation: DeltaW=eta*a*a^T is symmetric on reciprocally available endpoints with equal update factors.
symmetric_coactivity.consequence: That same-time product alone supplies no directional credit. Existing directed topology, different pre/post functions or states can create other asymmetries; this statement does not make the whole learned graph symmetric.
symmetric_coactivity.comparison: A causal preceding-state/observed-target update is explicitly asymmetric and must identify its two time roles.

causal_response_mixture.state: For post-token x_n=r*x_(n-1)+e_(token_n), the pre-input source at token n is c_n=sum_l>=1 r^l*e_(token_(n-l)), r=2^(-T/H).
causal_response_mixture.normalized_lag_mass: Normalizing the infinite linear sum gives weights (1-r)*r^(l-1). The latest token contributes1-r; the latest K contribute1-r^K.
causal_response_mixture.interpretation: Crediting present recurrent activity can mix associations from several lags. That may supply useful long context or unwanted associations; it is not automatically the immediately preceding token transition.
causal_response_mixture.cycle: In a repeated A,B,C sequence, before B arrives, the linear source amounts are A:r/(1-r^3), C:r^2/(1-r^3), B:r^3/(1-r^3). Relative to A, the other credits are r and r^2.
causal_response_mixture.cycle_limit: B-to-B means an association between token-related populations, not necessarily a self-edge on one neuron. Useful recurrent loops remain allowed; nonadjacent credit is not itself failure.

variable_timing.equation: For unequal gaps, each old input carries2^(-age/H); equal token order need not yield equal source credit.
variable_timing.distinction: One update per token removes repeated learning exposures caused by the number of frames. It does not remove timing dependence of the recurrent source state. Exact physical-time decay composes over subdivided frames in this scalar reference; finite writeback can break that equivalence.

alternatives.value: Uses the state that actually carries ongoing context without automatically adding a separate trace.
alternatives.compare: Pre-input matching and disambiguation, contamination by unobserved predictive alternatives, recurrence preservation and sensitivity to token spacing.
alternatives.limit: Current activity is not an oracle for which past observation should receive credit.

alternatives.source_basis: Independently established preceding observed contextual representation
alternatives.value: Can target an observed transition without treating generation fallback as teaching.
alternatives.compare: Learning unfamiliar transitions and retaining longer history across shared fragments.
alternatives.limit: The representation must actually be available at the update boundary. Two neural frames do not preserve an arbitrary previous token event; any extra retention needs demonstrated value and budget.

alternatives.source_basis: Temporally weighted changes or a narrower credit window
alternatives.value: May separate recent evidence from persistent background/context contributions.
alternatives.compare: Directionality versus loss of useful slow context, noise sensitivity, timing changes and low-precision update behavior.
alternatives.limit: For a known linear recurrence an innovation can subtract predictable decay, but that is not a valid general noise/causal decomposition after nonlinear recurrence or cancellation. No difference field, eligibility trace or time constant is selected.

empirical_scope: Compare the same real sequences at specified pacing and meaningful timing variation, holding neural dynamics and learning-exposure count explicit. Do not shorten useful recurrence merely to make a chosen credit heuristic resemble adjacency. Timing sensitivity can be intended behavior rather than an error; the comparison must state its prediction claim.
non_adoptions: No per-edge/per-neuron eligibility trace, token buffer, causal noise tag, baseline array, timer, winner store or new connection class.
No replacement of DMN/token repair by a flow rule, or selection of the independent training-state intervention.
No instantaneous symmetry requirement, fixed half-life, universal temporal kernel or requirement to remove small loops.
No SNN implementation/training, random neural simulation, benchmark, project tests, build, toolchain mutation, commit or push.

background_source_credit.status: exact conditional sampling and mean-update identities; no SNN training/simulation
background_source_credit.value_lineage: C15/P29 contextual prediction and C26/P60 useful history; P30 retained-source capacity dependency. H74 requires a demonstrated need before filters or state.

assumptions: One draw from currently eligible, absent endpoint IDs, with probability proportional to nonnegative source credit. Candidate counts are after any already-represented IDs are excluded.
Of307200 positive-credit candidates,6144 are informative by construction and have credit1. All other candidates have equal diagnostic credit b. Other CC cells may have zero credit.
The informative label is available to the arithmetic observer, not supplied to a runtime algorithm. No actual neural background distribution is assumed.
candidate_sampling.common_target_factor: A shared positive target factor e cancels from normalized sampling of e*c_i. It can gate or change the number of growth opportunities without changing their relative source probabilities. e=0 gives no distribution unless a separate rule specifies one.
candidate_sampling.limits: First-candidate law only. Without-replacement selection, retained endpoint exclusion and repeated learning change later draws and utility. This is not a false-connection rate measured in SNN data.

assumptions: Independent identically distributed exposures and fixed source/target roles, independent of the previous weight. The preceding informative indicator s predicts the later target y=s; no future token is exposed to the predictor.
Credit c=a when s=1 and c=b when s=0, with0<b<=a<=1. Target frequency is pi. Exact working/storage arithmetic, no growth or clipping.
Update w_next=w+eta*c*(y-w), with0<eta*a<=1. This is the earlier source-enabled affinity candidate, not a newly chosen learner.
source_enabled_mean_update.identity: At the fixed point of mean weight, E[w]=E[c*y]/E[c]=pi*a/(pi*a+(1-pi)*b). If c is constant, this is pi. If b=0 and pi*a>0, this is1.
source_enabled_mean_update.limits: Stationary mean of an ideal scalar learning reference, not its variance, convergence speed, network behavior or proof that the weight is a calibrated probability. Actual recurrent state can correlate noise with target/context.

background_source_credit.comparison_consequence: Assess source selection and learned predictive distinctions across the intended noise conditions and rare/shared contexts. Scalar magnitude alone does not identify the origin or future utility of a source contribution.
non_adoptions: No amplitude/density eligibility threshold, noise-origin tag, source trace, covariance estimator or extra matching state.
No automatic reuse of regime-classification filters for learning; useful weak context and predictive readiness remain allowed.
No changes to activity bounds, no-inhibitory-connection direction, static incoming slots, or DMN/token repair scope.

provenance.method: Exact rational mass ratios and independent expectation-balance checks over two exposure states.

prediction_horizon_reference.kind: Exact finite Markov-chain matrix arithmetic; no neural simulation or learning run
prediction_horizon_reference.purpose: Distinguish next-input readiness assessment from a longer-horizon predictive quantity without rejecting useful long-context recurrence.
prediction_horizon_reference.reference: Three abstract categorical states A->B->C, with C->C; P is row-stochastic. They are not semantic coordinates, neurons or an adopted source model.
definitions: M-I excludes the present state from discounted future occupancy.
The A row is (0,gamma,gamma^2/(1-gamma)); normalizing it yields (0,1-gamma,gamma), whereas the next-input distribution is (0,1,0).
The complete exact M and known gamma recover P=(I-M^(-1))/gamma. A raw occupancy row is not the same readout; this is not a claim that complete SR necessarily loses all one-step information.
prediction_horizon_reference.verification: Exact Fraction Gaussian elimination and both-sided inverse identities for all four discounts; separate geometric-series row identities; transition reconstruction checked.
prediction_horizon_reference.source_connection: MR-S090/MR-S091 define discounted future occupancy and specified neural learning realizations. This independent three-state example is not their empirical result.
prediction_horizon_reference.application_boundary: A correlation learned across overlapping responses can serve broader associations. Assessment must state its forecast horizon; a correctly learned broader statistic alone does not establish the provisional next-input matching objective.
non_adoptions: No successor matrix or inverse readout
No TD learner or reward objective
No probability interpretation of neuron rates
No selected discount or link to the isolated-token half-life
